provenance.run: stage 0, 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-17, against akholod/easy-cast-probe and akholod/easy-cast-probe-public
provenance.note: Every row below was produced by a real request. Anything not listed here is deliberately unmatched and resolves to endpoint_unavailable.

headers.Content-Type: <the media type, which must match the file extension>

wire.observedNote: Single phase. There is no policy call and no second host. The Content-Type header carries the declared type; a request without one was refused during exploratory work, though that exchange predates the observation log.
wire.sizeNote: The declared `size` query parameter is validated before the body is read: a request declaring 5 GiB while sending 64 bytes was refused 422 on size alone. An over-large file therefore costs one round trip, not one upload.

rows.observed: Returned identically for: a wrong repository_id, a repository we can read but cannot push to (cli/cli), and an omitted repository_id.
rows.why: Three different causes produce a byte-identical response. Naming one of them would be a guess presented as a diagnosis.

bodySignals: content_type is not included in the list of allowed content types
name has a file extension that does not match the content type
rows.observed: Both messages arrived together in errors[] in BOTH recorded cases: a .png declared as application/octet-stream, and a .log declared as text/plain. A single-reason 422 has not been observed.
rows.why: A body can carry more than one reason at once, so the message must be disjunctive rather than picking whichever matched first.

bodySignals: size Yowza that's a big file.
rows.observed: errors[0] = {resource: UserAsset, code: custom, field: size, message: "size Yowza that's a big file. Try again with a file size less than 10MB."}. Produced by declaring size=5368709120 while sending 64 bytes, so no asset was created.
rows.ceilingBytes: 10MB, stated by the endpoint itself; the unit (MB vs MiB) is not stated and was not measured.
rows.why: The endpoint names its own ceiling, and it enforces it on the declared size rather than on what was sent. The message is written for the web UI and carries HTML, which is stripped before the message reaches a caller — the wording is unchanged, only the markup goes.

default.why: Anything not matched above leaves the state of the remote side unknown. Uploads cannot be withdrawn, so an unrecognised answer is never guessed at and never retried.

unresolvedUnknowns: Abuse detection and rate limiting were not observed. A matrix of this size cannot trigger them, so a 403 with an HTML body remains possible and unclassified — it would resolve to endpoint_unavailable, which is the safe direction.
Behaviour with an installation token (ghs_) was not tested; CI is out of scope and GITHUB_TOKEN is deliberately never read.
A classic PAT without the repo scope was not tested — that credential has to be issued by hand.
Behaviour when the connection drops after the body has been sent was not induced deliberately; the transport treats it as request-started, which is the conservative reading.

.webm and .mov were not probed. .mp4 was: video/mp4 was accepted (201) on 2026-08-17 through the real CLI, and the bare URL rendered as a <video controls> player. Each further type would cost another permanent asset for a row the accept/reject shape already covers.

A 400 'Invalid Content-Type' was seen during exploratory work before recording began, and is NOT in observations.jsonl. It is therefore not a row here: a 400 falls to the default and is reported as endpoint_unavailable until it has been recorded properly.
